clue.text: Wicked girl caught in challenge — so reckless

indicators.note: in says the words before it are placed inside the word for challenge

parts.note: to dare someone is to challenge them
wicked means evil
May is a girl's name
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A naughty girl, caught up in some challenge, behaves recklessly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'caught' looks like part of the story, but it is the cricket abbreviation C; 'Wicked' is not the definition but a piece of the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone with a careless, rash attitude to danger is described by this phrase.

clue.text: Grace, Charlie's lover

definitions.meaning: Grace ... was the Victorian lighthouse keeper's daughter famed for a sea rescue
the old Jacobite song 'Charlie is my ...' gives Bonnie Prince Charlie a sweetheart

explanation.surface: Grace is named as the girlfriend of a man called Charlie.
explanation.walkthrough: Grace Darling, a lighthouse keeper's daughter, became a British heroine in 1838 by rowing out to rescue shipwreck survivors.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is the surname of the heroine Grace; the other is a term of endearment, as in the Scottish song about Prince Charlie.

clue.text: Hobo gets state allowance.

parts.note: VA is the abbreviation for Virginia, a US state
a grant is an allowance of money

explanation.surface: A tramp is living on a handout from the government.
explanation.definitionFit: A hobo is a wandering homeless person, a synonym.

clue.text: Degrees for this maybe from Eton guild

indicators.note: maybe from says the letters of the following words could be reworked to produce something else

explanation.surface: An old school society might be the source of a degree course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'maybe from' tells you to rearrange the letters of ETON GUILD.
explanation.definitionFit: Position east or west is measured in degrees on a globe, so this is something degrees are given for.

clue.text: Behind and right off beam

indicators.note: off says the letter for right comes away from the word for beam

parts.note: a rafter is a sloping roof beam

explanation.surface: Something at the back and to the right has fallen off a beam.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' removes R (right) from RAFTER.
explanation.definitionFit: Behind and this word are synonyms in the sense of later in time or following.

clue.text: Hire daily to empty rubbish initially

parts.note: a daily, or char, is a cleaning lady who comes in daily

indicators.note: initially says take the opening letter of each of the three words before it

explanation.surface: Take on a cleaning lady to empty the bins.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'daily' is British for a daily cleaner, also called a char.
explanation.definitionFit: To hire a boat or plane is to engage it for exclusive use, a synonym.

clue.text: Course in which knight upset Holy Roman emperor

indicators.note: upset in a down clue says the word for knight is turned upside down, read bottom to top

parts.note: Sir is the title of a knight
Otto was the name of several Holy Roman emperors

explanation.surface: A dinner course at which a knight overturned an emperor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns SIR to RIS.
explanation.definitionFit: A rice dish served as a course of a meal is an example.

clue.text: Jobs which turn quiet man into pest

indicators.note: turn says the letters that follow are to be turned about into a new order

parts.note: P, piano, is the musical abbreviation for quiet

explanation.surface: Some jobs make a quiet man become a nuisance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turn' rearranges P (quiet) with MAN INTO PEST, which read as a phrase looks like the result of the turning.
explanation.definitionFit: Jobs or posts filled by selection are a synonym.

clue.text: Model airborne soldier lost, we hear

indicators.note: we hear says the words before are judged by their sound when spoken

parts.note: a para is an airborne soldier, and lost means gone

explanation.surface: A model paratrooper has gone missing, so rumour has it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'we hear' turns PARA GONE into its sound-alike.
explanation.definitionFit: A model of excellence, an ideal example, is a synonym.

clue.text: Feature about partners not having arrived in this

indicators.note: about says the word for feature goes around the partners

parts.note: a trait is a feature or characteristic
N and S, North and South, are partners at the bridge table

explanation.surface: A trait concerning partners who have not yet arrived.
explanation.walkthrough: North and South sit as partners at the bridge table, which is why 'partners' gives two letters; the definition is a whole phrase meaning still travelling.
explanation.definitionFit: Goods or travellers still on their way are said to be in this state, so not yet arrived.

clue.text: Footballer there perhaps is over weight

indicators.note: is over in a down clue means the first piece sits above the second
perhaps says the word before could be a rearranged version of something else

parts.note: a quarter is an old weight, a quarter of a hundredweight

explanation.surface: A footballer standing there seems to be too heavy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' rearranges THERE to THREE. A quarter is an old British weight of 28 pounds. In rugby, a three-quarter is a back.
explanation.definitionFit: A rugby back, playing between the halves and full-back, is called this.

clue.text: Gold wise men returned, one concludes, in Japanese art

indicators.note: concludes says the letter for one comes at the end

parts.note: OR is gold in heraldry

indicators.note: returned says the word for wise men is read in reverse

parts.note: the Magi were the wise men from the East
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Gold and the returning Magi end up in a piece of Japanese art.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returned' turns MAGI to IGAM; 'concludes' puts I last.
explanation.definitionFit: The Japanese craft of folding paper into shapes is an example of a Japanese art.

clue.text: It turns this way and that

indicators.note: this way and that says the word reads the same in either direction

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: Something spins first one way, then the other.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is a palindrome, so it reads the same forwards and backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A device or muscle that spins something round is so called.

clue.text: Maud's black bat

parts.note: a quotation from Tennyson's poem Maud, 'For the black bat, ... has flown', naming the time of darkness as a bat

explanation.surface: A woman named Maud owns a dark-coloured bat.
explanation.walkthrough: Tennyson's 'Come into the garden, Maud' has the line 'For the black bat, night, has flown'.
explanation.definitionFit: In the poem the dark hours after sunset are pictured as a black bat flying.

clue.text: Suffered soldiers to be put back in dungeon, perhaps

indicators.note: in says the soldiers are placed inside the reworked dungeon
perhaps says dungeon is just one arrangement of these letters
put back says the letters for soldiers run backwards

parts.note: RE, the Royal Engineers, are soldiers

explanation.surface: Soldiers were made to suffer by being returned to a dungeon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' rearranges DUNGEON to UNDGONE, and 'put back' turns RE into ER; the Royal Engineers are the soldiers. The surface's dungeon is really anagram fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: To have undergone something is to have suffered or experienced it, a synonym.

clue.text: Takes steps-about-first feet, say

indicators.note: about says the word for takes steps goes around the word for first

parts.note: dances means takes steps on a dance floor
1st, written IST, is first

explanation.surface: Someone first takes action, then measures in feet.
explanation.walkthrough: First is written as 1st, read here in letters with I for 1. The definition is a sample: feet are one kind of distance.
explanation.definitionFit: Feet are an example of measured lengths or spans.

clue.text: Macbeth's employees who in the. : catalogue went for men.

definitions.text: Macbeth's employees who in the. : catalogue went for men

parts.words: Macbeth's employees who in the. : catalogue went for men
parts.note: Macbeth tells the hired killers of Banquo 'Ay, in the catalogue ye go for men', so these are the men he employs

explanation.surface: Macbeth's staff were listed as men in a catalogue.
explanation.walkthrough: In Shakespeare's play Macbeth hires killers for Banquo and, when they say they are men, replies 'Ay, in the catalogue ye go for men'.
explanation.definitionFit: Macbeth employed hired killers to dispatch Banquo.

clue.text: Get fence docked

indicators.note: docked says the word for fence loses its final letter, like a docked tail

parts.note: a fence, one who handles stolen goods, is a receiver

explanation.surface: Have a fence trimmed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'docked' cuts the last R from RECEIVER.
explanation.definitionFit: To get something is to be given or obtain it, a synonym.

clue.text: He's always difficult, says the Cockney

parts.note: ever means always

indicators.note: says the Cockney says the H is dropped, as London speech drops it

parts.note: hard means difficult

explanation.surface: A Londoner complains that some man is forever awkward.
explanation.walkthrough: 'says the Cockney' drops the H of HARD, giving 'ARD.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a man's given name, so a he.

clue.text: Scarf cuts out some of the traffic hum

indicators.note: cuts out some of says the answer is a run of letters lifted from inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Wearing a scarf blocks some of the noise of the traffic.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'Scarf cuts out' as the definition, but 'cuts out' belongs with 'some of' as the signal for the letters extracted.
explanation.definitionFit: A fichu is a light triangular shawl worn round the neck, a kind of neckerchief.

clue.text: Give money to — prospective bridegroom about noon:

indicators.note: about says the word for prospective bridegroom goes around noon

parts.note: a fiance is a man engaged to be married

explanation.surface: Pay a bridegroom-to-be around midday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts N inside FIANCE.
explanation.definitionFit: To fund a project is to supply cash for it, a synonym.

clue.text: Flag for a team member?.

definitions.meaning: a flag or standard carried by a regiment or ship
the cap, scarf or badge in a side's hues awarded to a player picked for a school or college team

explanation.surface: Is there a banner meant for one of the players?
explanation.walkthrough: In British schools and universities a player picked for a team is 'awarded' these, a cap or scarf in the team's hues.
explanation.definitionFit: A regiment's flag and a sporting team's award both go by this name.

clue.text: Annie wanders round about, coming from an old Bithynian city

indicators.note: round says the rearranged name goes around the word for about
wanders says the letters of Annie move about into a new order

parts.note: CA, circa, is the abbreviation for about

explanation.surface: Annie strolls about, having come from an ancient city in Asia Minor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wanders' rearranges ANNIE to NIEAN. Nicaea, of the Nicene Creed, was in Bithynia in modern Turkey.
explanation.definitionFit: Nicaea was an ancient city of Bithynia, so this adjective means belonging to it.

clue.text: Sibling's daughter in EEC resort

indicators.note: resort, read as re-sort, says the letters before are sorted again into a new order

explanation.surface: A family member stays at a holiday spot in the European Community.
explanation.walkthrough: 'resort' looks like a holiday place, such as Nice, but read as re-sort it rearranges IN EEC.
explanation.definitionFit: A brother's or sister's daughter is this relation, a straight description.

clue.text: Cancel a right in circular

parts.note: annul means cancel

explanation.surface: A circular letter announces the cancellation of a right.
explanation.definitionFit: Ring-shaped is the meaning, a synonym of circular.

clue.text: Pointed to accountant in malice

indicators.note: in says the accountant is placed inside the word for malice

parts.note: spite means malice
CA, chartered accountant, is the abbreviation for an accountant

explanation.surface: Someone gestured spitefully at an accountant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pointed' looks like a past verb with 'to', but it is a botanical adjective meaning spiky; 'to' is just a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A botanical term for something shaped like a spike, so pointed.

clue.text: Entertain various-NUJ members in the centre

indicators.note: in says the rearranged union is placed inside the word for centre

parts.note: the core is the centre

indicators.note: various says the letters following are mixed into a different order

parts.note: the NUJ, the National Union of Journalists, stands for its members

explanation.surface: Journalists in a union are entertained at the main venue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'various' rearranges NUJ to NJU. The NUJ is Britain's National Union of Journalists.
explanation.definitionFit: A conjuror entertains with magic tricks, so to perform such tricks is to entertain.

clue.text: No necessity to annoy craft head

parts.note: to needle someone is to annoy them
SS, steamship, is a craft
a ness is a headland

explanation.surface: There is no need to irritate the captain of a boat.
explanation.walkthrough: A ness is a headland, as in Loch Ness or Sheerness.
explanation.definitionFit: Lack of any need is the meaning, a synonym phrase.
